correctness.rationale: A complete proof fixes all allowed column types and computes the NODF paired-overlap numerator exactly. Optimization of unrestricted Barber vertex partitions reduces rigorously to independent choices for each column after splitting the two rows; the resulting global maximum is the stated quadratic. Monotonic NODF, concave modularity, and an exact final adjacent-class difference prove the full Pareto frontier and threshold for every n>=2 and 1<=c<n. Embedded independent exact checker verifies 9322 labeled small networks, 1927648 two-label assignments, and 198158 unrestricted set-partition evaluations; these finite tests corroborate but do not replace the universal proof.

originality.rationale: The original NODF and Barber source papers define separate indices, empirical ecology describes their relationships, and later software optimizes NODF numerically. None of the inspected primary sources or the semantic result comparisons states or implies the complete exact attainable two-index locus, all non-dominated two-row fixed-link classes, or the sharp common-maximizer inequality. Novelty is restricted to this exact finite-to-parametric synthesis, not the indices themselves or qualitative tension.
residual_risks: A broad extremal graph-optimization result for binary Ferrers matrices and bipartite modularity not returned by targeted searches might subsume a special case.

value.rationale: Ecological network analyses compare nesting and modular organization under fixed connectance; their objectives can be structurally incompatible. The theorem provides the entire attainable score locus and complete globally optimized Pareto set in the first nontrivial connected guild size, with an exact density threshold for perfect co-maximization rather than a heuristic witness or isolated numerical gain. This quantifies a meaningful constraint on metric-based network design and benchmarking.
